headline: 99 Lowell Street tower hearing closed, decision due at business meeting in two weeks; two subdivisions continued.
summary: Residents spoke against the 16-story tower with 196 apartments at 99 Lowell Street, mainly over losing about 200 public parking spaces on the Hartnett lot. The applicant also answered questions on sidewalks, bike storage, traffic, and a new parking garage.
decisions: Continued the subdivision hearing for 333 Coppas Avenue to December 3.
Continued the subdivision hearing for 1308 Wellington Road to December 3.
discussion: Lowell Street parking loss: Speakers said losing about 200 public spaces would hurt churches, local businesses, and older residents who walk to services. The applicant said the city chose to sell the lot and that a garage in the Pearl Street project would replace the spaces.
Tower height and sunlight: Speakers said the 16-story building would block views of the cathedral and cut sunlight. The applicant said its shade study showed little impact on the church.
Lowell Street parking options: Members and the applicant discussed angled parking, shared parking with churches, and a possible parking attendant on Sundays.
Wellington Road traffic: A neighbor asked for a wider traffic review. The applicant said the 16 lots would add traffic but not an adverse impact.

decision_evidence.quote: So I would like a motion from the board just to continue that hearing since we haven't accepted it yet. ... The motion carries and S2026-18 has been continued to our December 3rd, 2026 hearing.
So we will continue, let me make sure I read the case right, S2026-7 to our December 3rd public hearing.
